methodological_rigor.justification: The phase 1b/2 single-arm, open-label, multicenter design is appropriate for the coprimary safety and immunogenicity endpoints and employs a Simon's minimax two-stage design with pre-specified thresholds (target ≥75%, unacceptable ≤55%) and a Bayesian toxicity monitoring plan with explicit prior parameters, demonstrating formal planning. Sample size (45 enrolled, 37 immunogenicity-evaluable) exceeds the targeted 36 evaluable participants, and endpoints were pre-specified with validated grading (NCI CTCAE v5.0) and clear ELISpot positivity criteria. Statistical analyses are appropriate (Clopper–Pearson CIs, Mann–Whitney, Fisher's exact, Kruskal–Wallis), though multiplicity correction for the exploratory associations in Supplementary Table 2 is not reported, and the single-arm design precludes causal inference for the adenoma-related secondary endpoints (no concurrent control arm). The preclinical cytotoxicity component relied on PBMCs from a single participant (participant 12) with three technical replicates and limited biological replication, which is acknowledged as mechanistic proof-of-concept rather than robust validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual prospective single-arm (uncontrolled) interventional cohort trial, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b — it is a prospective phase 1b/2 study without randomization or concurrent control, which limits it below individual RCT (1b) status. Clinical relevance is high: Lynch syndrome affects ~1 in 300 individuals with up to 80% lifetime cancer risk and limited preventive options beyond surveillance and high-dose aspirin, making a tolerable off-the-shelf neoantigen vaccine with 100% immunogenicity response and durable 1-year immunity a credible foundation for cancer interception development. Endpoints are surrogate (safety, T cell immunogenicity) rather than cancer incidence, and the adenoma signal is exploratory, but the translational path to a randomized efficacy trial is clear and the mechanistic data (dextramer+ TemRA cells, cytotoxicity against CDC7-HCT116) strengthen the proof-of-concept.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this phase 1b/2 single-arm trial; a CONSORT flow diagram (Fig. 1b), protocol registration (NCT05078866), pre-specified coprimary endpoints, detailed eligibility criteria, AE grading per CTCAE v5.0, and screening-failure accounting are all reported. The protocol version history (v5, v5.3) is disclosed, and the Simon's two-stage statistical plan is pre-specified. Data availability includes referenced source data per figure and a public BioProject (PRJNA954699) for the external WES dataset; however, individual-participant trial data sharing and analysis code are not explicitly described (the Online content section is REDACTED), and detailed FSP sequences / HLA predictions are confined to Supplementary Table 3, limiting independent replication of the deconvolution pipeline.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily populational and translational: this is the first reported trial of the Nous-209 viral-vector FSP vaccine administered as monotherapy in healthy Lynch syndrome carriers for cancer interception, extending prior Nous-209 work in metastatic MMRd disease (ref 18) into a prevention setting. The platform itself (GAd/MVA encoding 209 FSPs) is not new, and prior LS neoantigen vaccine trials exist (Kloor 2020 with 3 FSPs; dendritic cell FSP vaccine), which limits conceptual/methodological novelty — the 209-neoAg breadth and demonstration of immunogenic FSPs in independent LS precancer datasets represent a meaningful empirical extension rather than a first-in-class concept. The positioning adequately acknowledges comparators (refs 10, 11, 18, 19) without over-claiming first-in-class status.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical flow from background through methods, results, and a measured discussion that explicitly addresses limitations (small sample, demographic homogeneity, specimen volume constraints, aspirin exclusion). The abstract is quantitatively grounded (n=45, 100% immunogenicity, 85% at 1 year, mean ~1,100 SFCs) and accurately mirrors the main findings. Acronyms are expanded on first use (LS, MSI, FSP, MMR, PBMC, SFC), figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable with explicit statistical tests, and the discussion appropriately distinguishes exploratory from pre-specified findings. Minor issues include a few awkward constructions (e.g., 'nave' for 'naïve', occasional run-on methods sentences) that do not impede comprehension.

key_strengths: Pre-specified Simon's minimax two-stage design with Bayesian toxicity monitoring and clear immunogenicity criteria; 100% ELISpot response at peak in all 37 evaluable participants with 85% durability at 1 year
Clinically important and underserved setting (Lynch syndrome cancer interception) with a credible translational path to a randomized efficacy trial
Mechanistic depth beyond primary endpoints: HLA-dextramer tracking of SPEF2-specific CD8+ TemRA cells, CD4/CD8 depletion to attribute responses, and CDC7-HCT116 microfluidic killing assay
Strong external validity signal — 94/115 immunogenic FSPs identified in-trial were present in an independent LS precancer/cancer dataset (PRJNA954699)
Transparent reporting with CONSORT flow diagram, protocol registration (NCT05078866), screening-failure accounting, and detailed AE tables
key_concerns: Single-arm, uncontrolled design precludes causal inference for the exploratory adenoma/advanced-adenoma secondary endpoints and the inverse correlation between reactive pools and adenoma presence
Demographic homogeneity (91% self-reported white, 56% male) limits generalizability across LS populations
Mechanistic cytotoxicity (CDC7-HCT116 killing) is anchored on PBMCs from a single participant (participant 12) with limited biological replication
No explicit multiplicity correction for the exploratory associations in Supplementary Table 2 (e.g., female vs male P=0.045)
Data/code availability is limited to figure source data and an external BioProject; individual-participant trial data sharing and analysis code are not explicitly described
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically rigorous, pre-specified phase 1b/2 proof-of-concept trial reporting a clean 100% immunogenicity rate with durable 1-year T cell responses, strong mechanistic validation, and a plausible interception signal in a high-impact LS prevention setting — characteristics consistent with a top-tier oncology journal; the uncontrolled design and exploratory efficacy signals warrant minor revisions rather than acceptance as-is.
